items.t: Data governance
items.x: Every critical data asset needs a named data owner. Governance is how you appoint them and keep them active.

items.t: Data cataloguing
items.x: Find the data other organisations depend on, and decide which of it is critical.

items.t: Data quality
items.x: Every critical data asset needs a data quality action plan (DQAP) or an equivalent.

items.t: Delivery and change
items.x: Embedding the DAM Policy in business as usual and in change programmes: business cases, assurance, legacy exits, contracts and handover.

items.t: Tools and interoperability
items.x: How catalogue, data quality, lineage, master data and governance tools work together, the open standards that connect them, and RFI questions to avoid...

items.t: Sector supplements
items.x: Sector supplements for health, social care, geospatial, statistics, data sharing, AI and more: governance overlays, catalogue fields and quality rule...

items.t: Start from your role
items.x: Routes through the DAM capability playbooks for chief data officers, coordinators, data owners, stewards, catalogue managers and analysts.

items.t: Learning
items.x: Short learning modules on the DAM Policy, data governance, cataloguing and data quality, with outcomes, activities and checks.

items.t: Library
items.x: Guidance, standards, templates and tools for data governance, data cataloguing and data quality, with open data downloads.

items.t: Working together
items.x: How data, records, security, digital, technology, analysis, commercial and delivery professionals can work together on critical data assets.

items.t: Capability model
items.x: Every capability the DAM Policy and related guidance need, flagged explicit, implicit or inferred, with a data maturity model and self-assessment.

items.t: Boards, councils and networks
items.x: Boards, councils and networks for data asset management in government: purpose, aims, outcomes, terms of reference and how to take part.

items.t: Sector supplement: Health and care data
items.x: For critical data assets that hold patient-level or care records. Adds the health roles, duties and coding standards the core playbooks do not cover.

items.t: Sector supplement: Adult and children's social care data
items.x: For assets built from council returns, such as adult social care client level data and children's social care census returns, where the source systems sit outside the policy's scope.

items.t: Sector supplement: Geospatial and address data
items.x: For assets that hold addresses, coordinates or map geometry. Adds geospatial metadata, open identifiers and positional quality.

items.t: Sector supplement: Official statistics and administrative sources
items.x: For assets used to produce official statistics. Joins the DQAP to quality assurance of administrative data, so quality is reported once for both purposes.

items.t: Sector supplement: Data sharing and legal gateways
items.x: For every critical data asset that includes personal data, because critical data assets are defined by being shared. Adds a legal gateway record to the governance and catalogue records.

items.t: Sector supplement: AI-ready data
items.x: For assets used, or likely to be used, for AI or automated decision support. Turns the GOV.UK AI-ready data guidance into checks at the annual review.

items.t: Sector supplement: Fraud and error
items.x: For assets used to detect fraud or error, where identity matching quality decides who is flagged.

items.t: Sector supplement: Justice, policing and national security
items.x: For assets in law enforcement, justice, defence or security settings, where only OFFICIAL assets are in scope and metadata itself may be sensitive.

items.t: Sector supplement: Data about people
items.x: For any asset that holds records about individual people. Makes sure forms and rules let people describe themselves accurately.

items.t: Sector supplement: Reference data and identifiers
items.x: For assets that depend on code lists and identifiers maintained by other organisations, such as area codes, organisation codes and company numbers.

items.t: Sector supplement: Records, retention and disposal
items.x: For every critical data asset that must be kept, archived or destroyed on a schedule. Joins data asset management to records management.

items.t: Sector supplement: Data architecture and models
items.x: For critical data assets whose structure others build on. Describes the entities, how they relate and which system is the authoritative source, and links them to the catalogue.

items.t: Sector supplement: Devolved governments and local government
items.x: For assets that flow to or from the devolved governments or councils, which are not bound by the policy but often depend on it.

items.t: Sector supplement: Environmental, sensor and time-series data
items.x: For monitoring and sensor data where readings arrive continuously and gaps, units and drift matter more than missing fields.

items.t: Sector supplement: Pupil and learner data
items.x: For assets about pupils and learners, which are long-lived and linked across schools, colleges and nations.

items.t: Learning module: The DAM Policy - what it asks of you
items.x: Explain who the policy applies to and what is in scope.

items.t: Learning module: Roles and accountability
items.x: Describe the data owner, data steward and data custodian roles.

items.t: Learning module: Setting up governance with five recipes
items.x: Run the Mandate, Frame, Assign, Operate and Assure recipes in order.

items.t: Learning module: Finding and designating critical data assets
items.x: Build a candidate list from existing registers.

items.t: Learning module: Describing assets with metadata others can use
items.x: Record the metadata properties in the GOV.UK guidance.

items.t: Learning module: Cataloguing, harvesting and reporting to GDS
items.x: Expose records so others can harvest them.

items.t: Learning module: Data quality foundations
items.x: Name the five principles and six dimensions of the Government Data Quality Framework.

items.t: Learning module: Building a DQAP and scoring issues
items.x: Write rules with targets from the issues framework.

items.t: Learning module: Running the three capabilities as one yearly cycle
items.x: Use the hand-offs so each fact is recorded once.

items.t: Learning module: Inclusive data practice
items.x: Apply equality and inclusion checks in each capability.

items.t: Learning module: Embedding the policy in delivery and change
items.x: Name the capabilities the policy relies on but does not state.

items.t: Learning module: What makes a critical data asset AI-ready
items.x: Name the four pillars in the GDS guidelines on AI-ready datasets.

items.t: Learning module: From FAIR to AI-ready metadata
items.x: Explain the four FAIR principles in plain English.

items.t: Learning module: Start from the question the data must answer
items.x: Write down the decision or question an AI use of an asset serves.

items.t: Learning module: Connecting data to AI with linked data, knowledge graphs and MCP
items.x: Explain the RDF triple and why linked data helps machines read metadata.

items.t: Learning module: Making public data AI-ready together
items.x: Look for existing work before building, across public sector code and catalogues.

items.t: Learning module: Governing AI use of critical data in practice
items.x: Run the AI-ready quality rules on a sample file.

items.t: Learning module: Leading data asset management - your first year
items.x: Set Must, Should and Could aims for your organisation and the outcomes each brings.

items.t: Learning module: Buying tools for data asset management without lock-in
items.x: Pick the requirements that fit the kinds of tool you need, with priorities.
